039/**
040 * Next-generation transport-agnostic REST client.
041 *
042 * <p>
043 * Create instances via {@link #create()} or {@link #builder()}:
044 * <p class='bjava'>
045 *    <jc>// Minimal — uses the built-in JDK HttpClient transport</jc>
046 *    RestClient <jv>client</jv> = RestClient.<jsm>create</jsm>();
047 *
048 *    <jc>// Explicit transport (e.g. for tests)</jc>
049 *    RestClient <jv>client</jv> = RestClient.<jsm>builder</jsm>()
050 *       .transport(<jv>mockTransport</jv>)
051 *       .header(<js>"Accept"</js>, <js>"application/json"</js>)
052 *       .build();
053 * </p>
054 *
055 * <p>
056 * By default, {@code RestClient} uses {@link JavaHttpTransport} (backed by the JDK's
057 * {@link java.net.http.HttpClient}), which ships built into the {@code juneau-rest-client} artifact and
058 * requires no extra dependencies on Java 11+.  Pulling in one of the optional transport modules
059 * ({@code juneau-rest-client-apache-httpclient-45}, {@code -apache-httpclient-50}, {@code -okhttp},
060 * {@code -jetty}) registers a higher-priority provider via {@link ServiceLoader} that takes
061 * over automatically.  An explicit {@link Builder#transport(HttpTransport)} call always wins.
062 *
063 * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
064 *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/NextGenRestClient">juneau-ng REST client</a>
065 * </ul>
066 *
067 * @since 9.2.1
068 */
069@SuppressWarnings({
070   "java:S1192", // Duplicated literals (argument/property names) read more clearly inline than as constants
071   "resource" // transport is closed in RestClient.close(); this class owns it
072})
073public final class RestClient implements Closeable {
074
075   /**
076    * Default body converters applied in order when {@link RestRequest#body(Object)} is called.
077    *
078    * <p>
079    * Custom converters registered via {@link Builder#bodyConverter(BodyConverter[])} are prepended to this list.
080    * Call {@link Builder#bodyConverters(BodyConverter[])} to replace all defaults.
081    */
082   public static final List<BodyConverter<?>> DEFAULT_BODY_CONVERTERS = List.of(
083      BodyConverter.of(HttpBody.class, TransportBody::of),
084      BodyConverter.of(InputStream.class, is -> TransportBody.of(StreamBody.of(is))),
085      BodyConverter.of(byte[].class, bytes -> TransportBody.of(ByteArrayBody.of(bytes))),
086      BodyConverter.of(File.class, file -> TransportBody.of(FileBody.of(file)))
087   );
088
089   final HttpTransport transport;
090   final List<HttpHeader> defaultHeaders;
091   final List<HttpPart> defaultQueryData;
092   final String rootUrl;
093   final List<RestCallInterceptor> interceptors;
094   final RichLogger debugLogger;
095   final RestClientDebugFormatter debugFormatter;
096   final List<BodyConverter<?>> bodyConverters;
097   final SerializerSet serializers;
098   final ParserSet parsers;
099   final Serializer defaultSerializer;
100   final Parser defaultParser;
101   final boolean allowPrivateUrls;
102   final RemoteUrlPolicy.AllowedRanges allowedAddressRanges;
103
104   private RestClient(Builder builder) {
105      this.transport = reqnn("transport",
106         builder.transport != null ? builder.transport : discoverTransport());
107      this.defaultHeaders = List.copyOf(builder.defaultHeaders);
108      this.defaultQueryData = List.copyOf(builder.defaultQueryData);
109      this.rootUrl = builder.rootUrl;
110      this.interceptors = buildInterceptors(builder);
111      this.debugLogger = RichLogger.getLogger(builder.debugLoggerName != null ? builder.debugLoggerName : RestClient.class.getName());
112      this.debugFormatter = builder.debugFormatter != null ? builder.debugFormatter : new BasicRestClientDebugFormatter();
113      this.bodyConverters = List.copyOf(builder.bodyConverters);
114      this.serializers = builder.serializers;
115      this.parsers = builder.parsers;
116      this.defaultSerializer = builder.defaultSerializer;
117      this.defaultParser = builder.defaultParser;
118      this.allowPrivateUrls = builder.allowPrivateUrls || Boolean.getBoolean(RemoteUrlPolicy.ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS_PROPERTY);
119      this.allowedAddressRanges = RemoteUrlPolicy.AllowedRanges.of(builder.allowedAddressRanges.toArray(new String[0]));
120   }
121
122   /**
123    * Builds the effective interceptor list, prepending the built-in {@code X-Request-Id} auto-send interceptor when
124    * {@link Builder#sendRequestId(boolean)} is enabled (the default).
125    *
126    * <p>
127    * The built-in runs first so its {@code onInit} stamps the id before any caller interceptor observes the request,
128    * and it is additive with {@link Builder#interceptors(RestCallInterceptor...)} rather than replacing it.
129    */
130   private static List<RestCallInterceptor> buildInterceptors(Builder builder) {
131      if (! builder.sendRequestId)
132         return List.copyOf(builder.interceptors);
133      var l = new ArrayList<RestCallInterceptor>(builder.interceptors.size() + 1);
134      l.add(new RequestIdInterceptor());
135      l.addAll(builder.interceptors);
136      return List.copyOf(l);
137   }

139   /**
140    * Returns the effective builder/settings-level {@code allowPrivateUrls} opt-in for this client (the logical OR
141    * of {@link Builder#allowPrivateUrls(boolean)} and the {@value RemoteUrlPolicy#ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS_PROPERTY}
142    * system property).
143    *
144    * <p>
145    * The fully effective per-call value additionally ORs in the {@code @Remote}/{@code @RemoteOp}
146    * {@code allowPrivateUrls} annotation attribute (see {@link Remote#allowPrivateUrls()}).
147    *
148    * @return {@code true} if this client opts into allowing private/loopback/link-local/metadata {@code @Remote} targets.
149    */
150   public boolean isAllowPrivateUrls() {
151      return allowPrivateUrls;
152   }
153
154   /**
155    * Returns the per-client special-purpose address ranges this client re-permits in the SSRF guardrail (see
156    * {@link Builder#allowAddressRanges(String...)}).  They are unioned with the
157    * {@value RemoteUrlPolicy#ALLOW_ADDRESS_RANGES_PROPERTY} system property at each check.
158    *
159    * @return The allowed ranges. Never <jk>null</jk>.
160    */
161   public RemoteUrlPolicy.AllowedRanges getAllowedAddressRanges() {
162      return allowedAddressRanges;
163   }

165   private static HttpTransport discoverTransport() {
166      // Lowest priority value wins; ties resolve to the first discovered provider.
167      return ServiceLoader.load(HttpTransportProvider.class).stream()
168         .map(ServiceLoader.Provider::get)
169         .filter(HttpTransportProvider::isAvailable)
170         .min(Comparator.comparingInt(HttpTransportProvider::getPriority))
171         .map(HttpTransportProvider::create)
172         .orElseGet(JavaHttpTransport::create);  // defensive fallback if META-INF/services was stripped (e.g. uber-jar shading)
173   }

256   public RestRequest request(String method, String url) {
257      reqnn("method", method);

273    * Returns the explicitly-configured default serializer used for outbound bodies when the format is not otherwise

280    * <p>
281    * <b>Beta — API subject to change:</b> This type is part of the next-generation REST client and HTTP stack.
282    * It is not API-frozen: binary- and source-incompatible changes may appear in the <b>next major</b> Juneau release
283    * (and possibly earlier).

285    * @return The configured default serializer, or {@link Optional#empty()} if none was set.
286    */

291   /**
292    * Returns the parser matching the given response {@code Content-Type}, or the explicitly-configured default parser.
293    *
294    * <p>
295    * Resolution precedence: an exact media-type match against the client's {@link ParserSet} wins; otherwise the
296    * explicitly-configured {@link Builder#defaultParser(Parser) default parser} is used; otherwise
297    * {@link Optional#empty()} is returned.  There is no implicit JSON fallback and no lone-registered-entry fallback,
298    * so a fully-unconfigured client resolves to empty (callers throw <c>415 Unsupported Media Type</c>).
299    *
300    * <p>
301    * <b>Beta — API subject to change:</b> This type is part of the next-generation REST client and HTTP stack.
302    * It is not API-frozen: binary- and source-incompatible changes may appear in the <b>next major</b> Juneau release
303    * (and possibly earlier).
304    *
305    * @param contentType The response {@code Content-Type} header value. May be <jk>null</jk>.
306    * @return The matching parser, or {@link Optional#empty()} if nothing matched and no default parser is configured.
307    */
308   public Optional<Parser> getMatchingParser(String contentType) {
309      if (parsers != null && contentType != null) {
310         var p = parsers.getParser(contentType);
311         if (p.isPresent())
312            return p;
313      }
314      return o(defaultParser);
315   }
316
317   /**
318    * Returns the registered request serializer matching the given media type, or {@link Optional#empty()} if none matches.
319    *
320    * <p>
321    * Unlike {@link #getDefaultSerializer()}, this method performs media-type-driven <i>selection</i> against the
322    * client's {@link SerializerSet} (via {@link SerializerSet#getSerializer(String)}) and returns
323    * {@link Optional#empty()} on no match so the caller can apply the locked no-match fallback (use the default
324    * serializer but still send the overridden {@code Content-Type} label).  An explicitly-configured single default
325    * serializer is also consulted when no set is registered.
326    *
327    * <p>
328    * <b>Beta — API subject to change:</b> This type is part of the next-generation REST client and HTTP stack.
329    *
330    * @param mediaType The desired request media type. May be <jk>null</jk>/empty.
331    * @return The matching serializer, or {@link Optional#empty()} if no registered serializer matches.
332    */
333   public Optional<Serializer> getSerializerForMediaType(String mediaType) {
334      if (mediaType == null || mediaType.isEmpty() || serializers == null)
335         return oe();
336      return serializers.getSerializer(mediaType);
337   }
338
339   /**
340    * Returns the registered parser matching the given media type, or {@link Optional#empty()} if none matches.
341    *
342    * <p>
343    * Used by the next-gen {@code RemoteClient} as the {@code accept} fallback parser: it is consulted only when the
344    * response {@code Content-Type} matched no registered parser (or the response was unlabeled).  Returns
345    * {@link Optional#empty()} on no match so the caller can fall back to the default parser.
346    *
347    * <p>
348    * <b>Beta — API subject to change:</b> This type is part of the next-generation REST client and HTTP stack.
349    *
350    * @param mediaType The desired parse media type. May be <jk>null</jk>/empty.
351    * @return The matching parser, or {@link Optional#empty()} if no registered parser matches.
352    */
353   public Optional<Parser> getParserForMediaType(String mediaType) {
354      if (mediaType == null || mediaType.isEmpty() || parsers == null)
355         return oe();
356      return parsers.getParser(mediaType);
357   }
358
359   /**
360    * Returns the default {@code Accept} header value advertising what this client can read.
361    *
362    * <p>
363    * <b>Beta — API subject to change:</b> This type is part of the next-generation REST client and HTTP stack.
364    * It is not API-frozen: binary- and source-incompatible changes may appear in the <b>next major</b> Juneau release
365    * (and possibly earlier).
366    *
367    * @return The default {@code Accept} header value, or <jk>null</jk> if no parsers and no default parser are
368    *    configured (no implicit {@code application/json} fallback).
369    */
370   public String getDefaultAccept() {
371      if (parsers != null) {
372         var mts = parsers.getSupportedMediaTypes();
373         if (! mts.isEmpty())
374            return mts.stream().map(MediaType::toString).collect(Collectors.joining(", "));
375      }
376      if (defaultParser != null) {
377         var mts = defaultParser.getMediaTypes();
378         if (! mts.isEmpty())
379            return mts.stream().map(MediaType::toString).collect(Collectors.joining(", "));
380      }
381      return null;
382   }

384   /**
385    * Creates a Java proxy for the given {@link Remote}-annotated interface.
386    *
387    * <p>
388    * Each method call on the returned proxy will be translated into an HTTP request using this client.
389    *
390    * <p class='bjava'>
391    *    UserService <jv>svc</jv> = client.remote(UserService.<jk>class</jk>);
392    *    String <jv>user</jv> = <jv>svc</jv>.getUser(<js>"42"</js>);
393    * </p>
394    *
395    * @param <T> The interface type.
396    * @param iface The interface class. Must be annotated with {@link Remote}. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
397    * @return A proxy instance backed by this client. Never <jk>null</jk>.
398    * @throws IllegalArgumentException If {@code iface} is not an interface or not annotated with {@code @Remote}.
399    */
400   public <T> T remote(Class<T> iface) {
401      return new RemoteClient(this).create(iface);
402   }

413   /**
414    * Fluent builder for {@link RestClient}.
415    *
416    * <p>
417    * <b>Beta — API subject to change.</b>
418    *
419    * @since 9.2.1
420    */
421   public static final class Builder {
422
423      HttpTransport transport;
424      final List<HttpHeader> defaultHeaders = l();
425      final List<HttpPart> defaultQueryData = l();
426      String rootUrl;
427      final List<RestCallInterceptor> interceptors = l();
428      RestClientDebugFormatter debugFormatter;
429      String debugLoggerName;
430      List<BodyConverter<?>> bodyConverters = new ArrayList<>(DEFAULT_BODY_CONVERTERS);
431      SerializerSet serializers;
432      ParserSet parsers;
433      Serializer defaultSerializer;
434      Parser defaultParser;
435      final List<Serializer> serializerList = l();
436      final List<Parser> parserList = l();
437      boolean allowPrivateUrls;
438      final List<String> allowedAddressRanges = l();
439      boolean sendRequestId = true;
440
441      private Builder() {}
442
443      /**
444       * Sets the HTTP transport to use.
445       *
446       * <p>
447       * If not set, {@link RestClient} discovers a transport via {@link ServiceLoader}.  When no
448       * sibling transport module is on the classpath, the built-in {@link JavaHttpTransport} (backed by the JDK's
449       * {@link java.net.http.HttpClient}) is used as the default.
450       *
451       * @param value The transport. Can be <jk>null</jk> (a transport is auto-discovered via {@link ServiceLoader}).
452       * @return This object.
453       */
454      public Builder transport(HttpTransport value) {
455         transport = value;
456         return this;
457      }
458
459      /**
460       * Sets a root URL prefix applied to all relative request URLs (those without {@code ://}).
461       *
462       * @param value The root URL (e.g. {@code "https://api.example.com/v1"}). May be <jk>null</jk>.
463       * @return This object.
464       */
465      public Builder rootUrl(String value) {
466         rootUrl = value;
467         return this;
468      }
469
470      /**
471       * Opts every {@code @Remote}/{@code @Url} call made through this client out of the default deny-private SSRF
472       * guardrail (see {@code org.apache.juneau.http.remote.RemoteUrlPolicy}), for local-dev/intranet targets that
473       * are intentionally private.
474       *
475       * <p>
476       * The effective per-call value is the logical OR of this setting, the
477       * {@value RemoteUrlPolicy#ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS_PROPERTY} system property, and the {@code @Remote}/{@code @RemoteOp}
478       * {@code allowPrivateUrls} annotation attribute: any one of the three opting in is sufficient. The {@code http}/
479       * {@code https} scheme requirement is unaffected.
480       *
481       * @param value {@code true} to allow private/loopback/link-local/metadata {@code @Remote} targets. Default {@code false}.
482       * @return This object.
483       */
484      public Builder allowPrivateUrls(boolean value) {
485         allowPrivateUrls = value;
486         return this;
487      }
488
489      /**
490       * Re-permits, for this client only, addresses that the default SSRF guardrail denies solely because they fall in
491       * one of the special-purpose ranges <c>192.0.0.0/24</c>, <c>198.18.0.0/15</c>, <c>224.0.0.0/4</c>,
492       * <c>240.0.0.0/4</c> or <c>ff00::/8</c> (for example a lab or appliance network on <c>198.18.0.0/15</c>).
493       *
494       * <p>
495       * This is the per-client counterpart of the {@value RemoteUrlPolicy#ALLOW_ADDRESS_RANGES_PROPERTY} system
496       * property and has exactly its narrow semantics: every entry (a CIDR range or a single address, parsed as a
497       * literal with no DNS lookup) must lie entirely inside one of those five ranges, and it never re-permits
498       * loopback, link-local/metadata (<c>169.254.169.254</c>), private, CGNAT or any other denied address.  It applies
499       * to the literal-host check, the connect-time (DNS-pinned) address selection and every redirect hop of this
500       * client's {@code @Remote} calls, on every first-party transport.
501       *
502       * <p>
503       * The effective allow-list is the <b>union</b> of these ranges and the system property's ranges (both are
504       * narrow, so the union is too).  Calls accumulate.  An invalid entry is reported by {@link #build()} as an
505       * {@link IllegalArgumentException}.
506       *
507       * @param value The CIDR ranges or single addresses to allow; each element may also hold several comma- or
508       *    whitespace-separated entries.  <jk>null</jk> or empty adds nothing.
509       * @return This object.
510       */
511      public Builder allowAddressRanges(String...value) {
512         if (value != null)
513            allowedAddressRanges.addAll(Arrays.asList(value));
514         return this;
515      }
516
517      /**
518       * Controls the built-in {@code X-Request-Id} auto-send interceptor (enabled by default).
519       *
520       * <p>
521       * When enabled, every request that does not already carry an {@code X-Request-Id} header (case-insensitive) is
522       * stamped with a freshly minted version-7 UUID before it is sent, and the server's echoed id is captured on the
523       * response ({@link RestResponse#getRequestId()}).  Set to {@code false} to disable the interceptor entirely:
524       * no id is sent or captured, and a later {@link #interceptors(RestCallInterceptor...)} call does not resurrect
525       * it.  Callers can still set an id per request via {@link RestRequest#requestId(String)}.
526       *
527       * @param value {@code false} to disable the auto-send interceptor. Default {@code true}.
528       * @return This object.
529       * @since 10.0.0
530       */
531      public Builder sendRequestId(boolean value) {
532         sendRequestId = value;
533         return this;
534      }
535

594      /**
595       * Adds one or more lifecycle interceptors called before/after each request.
596       *
597       * @param value The interceptors to add. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
598       * @return This object.
599       */
600      public Builder interceptors(RestCallInterceptor... value) {
601         interceptors.addAll(Arrays.asList(value));
602         return this;
603      }
604
605      /**
606       * Sets the formatter used for level-driven REST debug logging.
607       *
608       * <p>
609       * The formatter renders cumulative content based on the resolved debug logger level:
610       * <ul>
611       *    <li>{@link Level#INFO INFO} - basic line ({@link RestClientDebugFormatter#formatBasic(RestRequest, RestResponse)}).
612       *    <li>{@link Level#FINE FINE} - basic + headers.
613       *    <li>{@link Level#FINEST FINEST} - basic + headers + body.
614       * </ul>
615       *
616       * @param value The formatter. Can be <jk>null</jk> to restore the default formatter.
617       * @return This object.
618       */
619      public Builder debugFormatter(RestClientDebugFormatter value) {
620         debugFormatter = value;
621         return this;
622      }
623
624      /**
625       * Sets the logger name used for REST debug records.
626       *
627       * <p>
628       * If not set, defaults to {@code RestClient.class.getName()}.
629       *
630       * @param value The logger name. Can be <jk>null</jk> to use the default logger name.
631       * @return This object.
632       */
633      public Builder debugLoggerName(String value) {
634         debugLoggerName = value;
635         return this;
636      }
637
638
639      /**
640       * Prepends custom body converters to the default converter list.
641       *
642       * <p>
643       * Custom converters are checked before the defaults when {@link RestRequest#body(Object)} is called.
644       *
645       * @param value The converters to prepend. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
646       * @return This object.
647       */
648      public Builder bodyConverter(BodyConverter<?>... value) {
649         var prepended = new ArrayList<BodyConverter<?>>(Arrays.asList(value));
650         prepended.addAll(bodyConverters);
651         bodyConverters = prepended;
652         return this;
653      }
654
655      /**
656       * Replaces the entire body converter list (including defaults).
657       *
658       * <p>
659       * Use this when you want full control over body conversion, including disabling the built-in defaults.
660       *
661       * @param value The complete replacement converter list. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
662       * @return This object.
663       */
664      public Builder bodyConverters(BodyConverter<?>... value) {
665         bodyConverters = list(value);
666         return this;
667      }
668
669      /**
670       * Sets the serializer registry used for outbound bodies.
671       *
672       * @param value The serializer set. May be <jk>null</jk>.
673       * @return This object.
674       */
675      public Builder serializers(SerializerSet value) {
676         serializers = value;
677         return this;
678      }
679
680      /**
681       * Sets the parser registry used for inbound bodies.
682       *
683       * @param value The parser set. May be <jk>null</jk>.
684       * @return This object.
685       */
686      public Builder parsers(ParserSet value) {
687         parsers = value;
688         return this;
689      }
690
691      /**
692       * Appends serializers (built into a {@link SerializerSet} at build time if no set was supplied).
693       *
694       * @param value The serializers to append. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
695       * @return This object.
696       */
697      public Builder serializer(Serializer... value) {
698         serializerList.addAll(Arrays.asList(value));
699         return this;
700      }
701
702      /**
703       * Appends parsers (built into a {@link ParserSet} at build time if no set was supplied).
704       *
705       * @param value The parsers to append. Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
706       * @return This object.
707       */
708      public Builder parser(Parser... value) {
709         parserList.addAll(Arrays.asList(value));
710         return this;
711      }
712
713      /**
714       * Designates the default serializer used for outbound bodies when no registered serializer matches the
715       * requested media type.
716       *
717       * <p>
718       * This is the explicit, opt-in way to restore a fallback serializer.  Without it, a request that cannot be
719       * matched to a registered serializer (and any body requiring serialization on a serializer-less client) fails
720       * rather than silently defaulting to JSON.  Set {@code defaultSerializer(JsonSerializer.DEFAULT)} to recover
721       * the pre-10.0 implicit-JSON behavior.
722       *
723       * @param value The default serializer. May be <jk>null</jk>.
724       * @return This object.
725       */
726      public Builder defaultSerializer(Serializer value) {
727         defaultSerializer = value;
728         return this;
729      }
730
731      /**
732       * Designates the default parser used when the response {@code Content-Type} is absent or matches no registered
733       * parser.
734       *
735       * <p>
736       * This is the explicit, opt-in way to restore a fallback parser.  Without it, a response whose
737       * {@code Content-Type} matches no registered parser fails with <c>415 Unsupported Media Type</c> rather than
738       * silently parsing as JSON.  Set {@code defaultParser(JsonParser.DEFAULT)} to recover the pre-10.0
739       * implicit-JSON behavior.
740       *
741       * @param value The default parser. May be <jk>null</jk>.
742       * @return This object.
743       */
744      public Builder defaultParser(Parser value) {
745         defaultParser = value;
746         return this;
747      }
748
749      /**
750       * Builds and returns the {@link RestClient}.
751       *
752       * @return A new instance. Never <jk>null</jk>.
753       */
754      public RestClient build() {
755         if (serializers == null && ! serializerList.isEmpty())
756            serializers = SerializerSet.create().add(serializerList.toArray(new Serializer[0])).build();
757         if (parsers == null && ! parserList.isEmpty())
758            parsers = ParserSet.create().add(parserList.toArray(new Parser[0])).build();
759         return new RestClient(this);
760      }
761   }
762}
